llm.summary: The skill is mostly transparent and consent-based, but it contradicts its own local-only storage guarantee by allowing generated skills to be installed into `skills/` or published externally.

dimensions.detail: Reads and writes are generally limited to project-local `.learnings/`, with sanitization and user confirmation, but generated drafts may contain content derived from local records and later leave the local boundary if published.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown documentation and a normal install command; I found no executable installer, hooks, scripts, dependencies, or remote payload execution in the inspected artifact files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact repeatedly says it only writes under `.learnings/` and never modifies other Skills, while the synthesis workflow offers saving generated output to `skills/` and publishing with `clawhub skill publish` after confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persisting generated Skills into `skills/` can affect future agent behavior; this is disclosed in one workflow but conflicts with the stronger storage and no-other-skill-modification guarantees.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The self-improvement purpose fits recording lessons, errors, exports, and analytics, but smart skill synthesis can turn stored learning records into active Skill instructions and optionally publish them, which is a higher-impact capability than ordinary note-taking.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local learning records being used to generate future Skill drafts. Before approving any generated skill installation or ClawHub publication, review the full draft for commands, file paths, credentials, network behavior, and instructions copied from past conversations. Treat the advertised `.learnings/`-only guarantee as incomplete because the artifact also documents writes to `skills/` and external publishing.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a real review concern: SKILL.md allows generated drafts to be saved to `skills/` despite claiming `.learnings/` is the only write directory.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the local-only guarantees are materially inconsistent with install and publish options.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in downgraded form: publication is opt-in and disclosed, but it is still under-scoped because learning-derived content may be externally distributed.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a medium review concern rather than malicious behavior: crossing from `.learnings/` into `skills/` requires user confirmation but violates the advertised storage boundary.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a concern: the workflow can derive triggers and operating procedures from conversation-derived learning records without documented semantic validation against prompt injection or unsafe instructions.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the `.env` reference appears inside an example checklist about reading environment variables from `.env` rather than hardcoding; it is not an instruction to steal or access credentials.
[EA2] expected: Mostly downgraded: the artifact repeatedly requires user confirmation and says improvements are not auto-executed, though generated skill installation remains a separate persistence concern.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language usage and instructions affect accessibility and clarity, but do not create a security issue by themselves.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a minor contributing concern: broad phrases like `记下来` and `怎么改进` could trigger persistence unintentionally, though the skill requires confirmation before writes.
[RP1] expected: Downgraded: the Docker reference is an illustrative generated-skill example and not a dependency or runnable image in this package.
[EA3] expected: Downgraded: the MIT license language is standard licensing text and not evidence of runtime scope creep.
